1995

Completed F.Sc (Pre-medical) with a strong focus on Biology, Chemistry, and Physics, laying a solid foundation in scientific principles and research methodologies.

Experience

2023 - Current
SellEton Scales | Liberty Scales - United States

Ecommerce Manager

As an E-commerce Manager and Shopify Expert, I manage daily operations, oversee product listings and promotions, and analyze data to enhance SEO and SEM strategies, boosting traffic and conversions. I design and optimize shopping experiences, enhancing customer satisfaction and loyalty, collaborate with teams to drive sales, and track industry trends for strategic insights.
2023 - Current
SellEton Scales | Liberty Scales - United States

Digital Content Manager

Job Duties: Building and managing Shopify stores, ensuring a seamless online shopping experience. Managing various social media accounts, including a YouTube channel, to enhance brand presence and engagement. Creating and editing videos, tailoring content to resonate with diverse audiences. Designing brochures, catalogs, and other print materials, combining creativity with brand messaging for impactful visuals.
Since 2023
HueBlue - Pakistan

WordPress Developer

Job Duties: WordPress development, including theme customization, plugin integration, and SEO optimization. Ensuring responsive, user-friendly designs with regular updates for security and optimal performance across all devices and browsers.
Since 2020
Adjuster University - United States

Video Editor

Job Duties: Editing and producing high-quality video content for online courses, ensuring clarity and engagement. Responsible for overseeing and managing the Adjuster University YouTube channel, including video editing, content scheduling, audience interaction, and channel optimization.
Since 2019
Naomi Peris - Australia

Video Editor

Job Duties: Crafting and refining video content to high standards, focusing on clear communication and audience engagement. Tasked with the effective management of the Adjuster University YouTube channel, encompassing content planning, video editing, audience engagement, and channel growth strategies.
Since 2019
ShahzadSadiq.com

Freelance Digital Designer

Job Duties: Creating visually engaging designs for digital and print media, and expert in WordPress website development and customization. Producing and editing videos for various platforms, ensuring content is engaging, informative, and aligned with brand identity. Refining audio content for podcasts, focusing on clear sound quality and compelling narrative flow. Crafting and editing short-form video content specifically for social media platforms, tailored to increase viewer engagement and maintain brand consistency. Designing, customizing, and maintaining WordPress websites, including theme customization, plugin integration, and ensuring cross-platform compatibility. Best practices in web design and performing regular site updates and maintenance for optimal performance and security. Extensively worked on diverse online platforms including Upwork.com, Fiverr.com, Freelancer.com, and Guru.com, showcasing a broad range of digital design skills and project versatility.
2023
The Balanced Practice - Canada

Podcast Editor

Job Duties: Editing audio for podcasts, ensuring clear sound quality and engaging storytelling. Editing short-form video content tailored for various social media platforms, focusing on viewer engagement and brand consistency.
2020 - 2023
SellEton Scales - United States

Social Media Manager | Video Editor | Graphic Designer

Job Duties: Managing social media strategy and content, expert video editing for impactful storytelling, and designing visually appealing graphics to strengthen brand identity across digital platforms.
2021 - 2023
Duo Finance - Australia

Graphic Designer | Video Editor

Job Duties: Crafting engaging visual designs for multiple platforms, encompassing both digital and print formats. Executing all stages of video production, from initial cutting to final edit, ensuring content is both engaging and informative.
2019 - 2023
Blue Crane Capital - Australia

Graphic Designer | Video Editor

Job Duties: Creating visually appealing designs for a variety of mediums, including digital and print materials. Cutting, editing, and producing video content that engages and informs the audience effectively.

Have you ever dreamed of writing amazing stories, articles, or blogs and getting paid for it but worried because you don’t have any experience? Don’t worry! You’re about to discover that starting a career in freelance writing is not only possible but also exciting, even if you’re just beginning.

In this guide, we’ll walk through the steps to kick off your writing journey, from understanding what freelance writing is all about to making your very own portfolio, finding your first writing gigs, and even managing your earnings like a pro.

I know it might seem a bit scary at first, like the first time you ride a bike without training wheels, but trust me, with some practice and the right tips, you’ll be cruising in no time. So, let’s dive in and turn your writing dreams into reality!

Table of Contents

  • Understanding the Basics of Freelance Writing
  • How To Become A Freelance Writer With No Experience: Getting Started
  • Creating an Impressive Portfolio Without Experience
  • Finding Your First Freelance Writing Opportunities
  • Building Your Brand and Online Presence
  • Enhancing Your Skills Through Education and Practice
  • Setting Rates and Managing Finances as a New Freelancer
  • Overcoming Common Challenges Faced by New Freelancers
  • Conclusion

Understanding the Basics of Freelance Writing

What is Freelance Writing?

Freelance writing is like being your boss, but for writing! You get to write articles, stories, or even posts for websites, all on your terms. It’s not like a regular job where you visit an office daily. Instead, you choose what you want to write about and who you want to write for. It’s a great way to turn your love for writing into a fun job.

Different Kinds of Freelance Writing

There are so many ways you can write as a freelancer:

  • Blogging: Writing cool posts for blogs, sharing your thoughts, or teaching something new.
  • Copywriting: This is when you write to help companies sell things, like making a toy sound super exciting.
  • Content Writing: This involves creating articles or posts that give people helpful information, like how to bake a cake or care for a pet.

Skills Every Freelance Writer Needs

To be a great freelance writer, you need a few key skills:

  • Good Writing: You should be able to write clearly and make your writing interesting.
  • Creativity: Developing new ideas or fun ways to say things is important.
  • Research Skills: Sometimes, you must learn about new things and write about them well.
  • Being Organized: Keeping track of all your writing jobs and doing them on time is super important.

Remember, these skills get better the more you practice. It’s like learning to play a new game – the more you play, the better you get!

Why Is Freelance Writing Awesome?

Freelance writing is awesome because you can:

  • Work from Anywhere: You can write from your bedroom, a café, or even a park!
  • Choose What You Write About: Love video games or fashion? You can write about what interests you.
  • Be Your Boss: No need to follow strict rules or have a boss telling you what to do.

How To Become A Freelance Writer With No Experience: Getting Started

Finding Your Special Writing Area

Think of something you enjoy or know a lot about. This could be your favorite hobby, like playing video games, cooking, or even dinosaurs! This special area is called your ‘niche.’ Writing about what you love or know well is easier and a lot more fun. It’s like sharing a piece of your world with others through your words.

Skills to Shine in Writing

Even if you’re just starting, having good writing skills is like having a superpower. Here’s how to make your writing shine:

  • Practice Makes Perfect: Write a little every day. It’s like practicing a sport or a musical instrument.
  • Read a Lot: Reading books, blogs, or anything else helps you understand different writing styles.
  • Learn the Basics: Understand grammar rules and how to structure your writing. It’s like learning the rules of a game.

Tools for a Freelance Writer

Just like a painter needs brushes, a freelance writer needs some tools. These include:

  • A Good Computer or Laptop: This is where you’ll do most of your writing.
  • Writing Software: Programs like Microsoft Word or Google Docs.
  • A Notebook: Great for jotting down ideas when they pop into your head.
  • Internet Access: For research and finding writing jobs.

These tools are your treasure chest, helping you create and share your stories and ideas.

Learning Never Stops

The best writers are always learning. You can:

  • Join Writing Workshops: These are fun classes to learn new writing tricks.
  • Read Writing Blogs: Many experienced writers share tips on their blogs.
  • Ask for Feedback: Show your writing to friends or family and see what they think. It’s like getting a high-five and advice at the same time.

Creating an Impressive Portfolio Without Experience

What’s a Portfolio, and Why Do You Need One?

Imagine a portfolio as your treasure chest, where you keep all your best writing. When people want to hire a writer, they like to see this treasure chest to know how good the writer is. Even if you’re starting, you can fill your chest with awesome writing pieces that show off your skills.

Making Writing Samples from Scratch

  • Start Writing Now: Pick topics you love and start writing about them. These can be short stories, articles, or even blog posts.
  • Fake Projects are OK: You can create a company and write something for it, like an ad or a website page.
  • Keep It Diverse: Try writing different things. It shows you’re good at more than one type of writing.

Each piece you write is like a shiny gem you add to your treasure chest.

Using Blogs and Guest Posts

  • Start Your Own Blog: It’s like having your little corner online. Write about what interests you.
  • Guest Post on Other Blogs: Some blogs let you write for them. It’s like being invited to a friend’s house to share a story.

These are great ways to get your writing out there and add more gems to your portfolio.

Showcasing Your Work

  • Make It Look Good: Arrange your writing samples so they’re easy to read and look nice.
  • Tell the Story Behind Each Piece: For each sample, write a little about why you wrote it or what you learned from it.
  • Be Proud of Your Work: Even if you’re just starting, be proud of your writing. It shows confidence.

Finding Your First Freelance Writing Opportunities

Where to Look for Writing Jobs

Starting your hunt for writing jobs is like going on a treasure hunt. Here are some cool places to start looking:

  • Job Boards: Websites like ProBlogger and Indeed post lots of writing jobs.
  • Freelance Platforms: Sites like Upwork and Fiverr are big marketplaces for freelance work.
  • Social Media: Job offers are sometimes hidden in places like LinkedIn or Twitter.

Think of these as maps that lead to hidden writing treasures.

Navigating Job Boards and Freelance Platforms

  • Create a Profile: Share a bit about yourself and show off your portfolio.
  • Search Smartly: Use keywords that match your writing interests, like ‘sports writer’ or ‘fashion blogger.’
  • Apply Often: The more jobs you apply for, the better your chances of finding one. It’s like casting a wide net to catch fish.

Every job you apply for is a step closer to finding your perfect writing gig.

Crafting Winning Proposals and Pitches

  • Be Clear and Concise: When you write to a potential client, be clear about what you can do for them. It’s like telling someone why you’d be a great teammate.
  • Show Your Passion: Let your excitement for writing shine through.
  • Tailor Each Pitch: Make each proposal special for your applying job, like picking out a gift perfect for a friend.

Writing a great proposal is like making a key that unlocks the door to new writing jobs.

Networking: Making Connections

  • Join Writing Groups: Online groups or forums are great places to meet other writers and learn about job opportunities.
  • Attend Workshops or Webinars: Here, you can learn new things and meet people needing a writer.
  • Ask for Referrals: If someone likes your writing, they might tell others about you.

Networking is like making friends who can help you on your writing journey.

Building Your Brand and Online Presence

Creating Your Writer’s Website

Having your own website is like having a digital home for your writing. It’s a place where people can come and see all the cool things you’ve written. Here’s how to make it awesome:

  • Keep It Simple and Neat: Make sure your website is easy to navigate, like a clear path through a garden.
  • Show Off Your Best Work: Put your best writing pieces front and center, like displaying trophies in a showcase.
  • Tell Your Story: Share a bit about yourself – who you are, why you love writing, and what you can offer. It’s like introducing yourself to new friends.

Using Social Media Wisely

Social media is like a giant party where you can meet many people. Use it to show your writing and connect with others:

  • Pick the Right Platforms: Whether it’s Twitter, Instagram, or LinkedIn, find out where your potential readers and clients hang out.
  • Share Your Work and Thoughts: Post about your latest writing or share tips you’ve learned. It’s like sharing fun facts with friends.
  • Engage with Others: Comment on other people’s posts and join conversations. It’s about making friends in the big online world.

The Power of Personal Branding

Your brand is like your unique stamp. It’s what makes you different from other writers:

  • Be Consistent: Use the same style and voice in your writing, website, and social media. It’s like wearing your favorite color so people recognize you.
  • Show Your Personality: Let your unique self shine through in your writing and online presence. It’s like showing off your style.
  • Keep It Professional: Remember, everything you post is like a message to potential clients, so keep it friendly and professional.

Enhancing Your Skills Through Education and Practice

Online Courses and Webinars: Learning from the Pros

Think of online courses and webinars as secret maps leading to the treasure of knowledge. They’re like classes where you can learn new writing tricks from professionals:

  • Find Courses That Excite You: Look for courses about types of writing you love or want to learn more about.
  • Join Webinars: These mini-classes online where experts discuss cool writing tips.
  • Keep Learning: Always be on the lookout for new things to learn. It’s like adding new tools to your writing toolbox.

Reading Writing Blogs: Tips from Fellow Writers

Writing blogs are like diaries of other writers where they share their secrets. By reading them, you can:

  • Learn from Their Experiences: Find out what works and what doesn’t in writing.
  • Get Inspired: Their stories and tips can sometimes spark new ideas in your writing.
  • Stay Updated: Writing trends change, so reading blogs helps you keep up with what’s new.

Getting Feedback: Growing Through Comments

Feedback is like a mirror showing how your writing looks to others. Here’s how to use it to grow:

  • Ask Family or Friends: Show them your writing and ask what they think.
  • Join Writing Groups: Share your work with other writers and listen to their suggestions.
  • Learn from Critiques: Don’t get sad if someone points out a mistake. It’s like finding a shortcut in a game that helps you play better.

Keep Writing: Practice Makes Perfect

The best way to get better at writing is to write! It’s like practicing a sport or playing an instrument:

  • Write Regularly: Make it a habit to write something every day, even if it’s just a little.
  • Try Different Styles: Experiment with writing different things. It’s like playing different roles in a play.
  • Challenge Yourself: Set small goals, like writing a story in a week or a blog post in a day.

Setting Rates and Managing Finances as a New Freelancer

Understanding Market Rates for Writing

Setting your rates as a new writer is like deciding the price of lemonade at your stand. You don’t want it too high or too low. Here’s how to figure it out:

  • Research: Look at what other writers charge. It’s like checking the prices at other lemonade stands.
  • Start Reasonable: Begin with a rate that feels fair for your skills, but don’t sell yourself too short.
  • Adjust as You Grow: As you get better and more known, you can slowly raise your rates.

Tips on Setting Your Rates

  • By the Hour or Project: Decide if you want to charge by the hour or each writing piece.
  • Be Clear with Clients: When you talk to someone who might hire you, be clear about how much you’ll charge. It avoids surprises later, like a hidden cost in a game.

Negotiating with Clients

  • Be Ready to Talk About Money: Don’t be shy about discussing your rates. It’s part of being a freelance writer.
  • Know Your Worth: Believe in the value of your work. It’s like knowing you have a winning hand in a card game.
  • Be Flexible but Firm: It’s okay to adjust a little, but don’t let anyone make you feel your work isn’t worth much.

Managing Your Freelance Finances

Handling your money well is super important when you’re a freelancer:

  • Keep Track of Your Earnings: Write down how much money you make, like keeping score in a game.
  • Save for Taxes: Remember, you’ll have to pay taxes on your earnings, so put some money aside.
  • Plan for Slow Times: Sometimes work might be slow, so having some savings is good.

Overcoming Common Challenges Faced by New Freelancers

Dealing with Rejection: It’s Not the End

Getting rejected is like losing a level in a video game. It’s not fun, but it’s part of the journey. Here’s how to handle it:

  • Don’t Take It Personally: Remember, it’s not about you; it’s just that your writing wasn’t the right fit this time.
  • Learn from It: Try to find out why you were rejected. It’s like getting clues to do better next time.
  • Keep Trying: The more you try, the better your chances. Don’t give up after one ‘no’.

Time Management: Balancing Your Writing Life

Managing your time well is like juggling. You need to keep all your balls in the air:

  • Make a Schedule: Plan your day like a fun outing. Set aside specific times for writing, researching, and taking breaks.
  • Avoid Procrastination: Don’t put off writing. It’s like waiting until the last minute to do your homework.
  • Use Tools to Help: Some apps and tools can remind you when to work and when to take a break.

Balancing Client Expectations with Personal Growth

Sometimes, clients want things done a certain way, which might not match your style. It’s like trying to fit a square peg in a round hole:

  • Communicate Clearly: Talk to your clients about what they want and what you can do. It’s like making sure everyone is playing the same game.
  • Be Flexible, but Stay True to Yourself: It’s okay to try new things but keep your voice and style.
  • Keep Learning: The more you learn, the easier it becomes to adapt to different clients’ needs.

Conclusion

As you embark on your freelance writing journey, remember your passion for writing is your strongest asset. From understanding the basics of freelance writing to building a captivating portfolio, each step is an opportunity to grow. Embrace the challenge of finding your first gigs, and use your online presence to showcase your unique voice. Never stop learning and refining your skills – every piece you write is a step toward mastery. Setting your rates and managing your finances marks the transition from hobby to profession. Overcoming challenges along the way will only make you stronger. Now, take these insights and turn them into action. Your journey as a freelance writer is not just about finding work; it’s about realizing your dreams. Write with heart, learn enthusiastically, and build your path to success. The world of freelance writing awaits you!

Who we are

Our website address is: https://shahzadsadiq.com.

What personal data we collect and why we collect it

Comments

When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Contact forms

Cookies

If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Analytics

Who we share your data with

How long we retain your data

If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where we send your data

Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

Your contact information

Additional information

How we protect your data

What data breach procedures we have in place

What third parties we receive data from

What automated decision making and/or profiling we do with user data

Industry regulatory disclosure requirements
